title: Riesz representation and approximation by continuous functions
summary: Integration as a positive linear functional and the Riesz representation theorem for positive linear functionals; the Lebesgue integral as the completion of the Riemann integral; Lusin's theorem and the Vitali–Carathéodory theorem; approximation of measurable functions by continuous ones; convergence almost everywhere and the convergence theorems under a.e. hypotheses; countable additivity of the integral.

preparation.description: Read lecture 10: integration as a linear functional, the Riesz representation theorem for positive linear functionals, the Lebesgue integral as the completion of the Riemann integral.
Read lecture 11: Lusin's theorem and the Vitali–Carathéodory theorem.
Read lecture 12: approximation by continuous functions, convergence almost everywhere, convergence theorems for a.e. convergence, countable additivity of the integral.
